title: Predictable-quality hosted endpoints — evaluation-gated PRD and canary launch checklist
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Goal: Ship a minimal, unified hosted endpoint suite (text-generation/chat, embeddings, rerank) that guarantees predictable output quality using an evaluation-gated rollout. This PRD captures measured acceptance gates (quality and infra), operational runbook items, and a staged canary plan tied to automated evals so we can safely replace legacy endpoints without regressing customer-facing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: Single hosted endpoint surface supports chat/completions/embeddings/rerank with consistent routing and documented request/response contracts for each mode.

Quality: For each workload (chat, completion, embeddings, rerank) we define a reference eval suite and require no more than 2% relative degradation vs the current GA baseline on key metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-style proxies for gen, cosine-sim recall@1 for embeddings, rerank@N for rerank).
Latency: P95 token-latency for generation endpoints <= 350ms on standard lane; embeddings P95 <= 120ms for 768-dim vectors; overall request P99 error rate < 0.5% across canary slices.
Reliability: Canary run must show zero severity-1 incidents and demonstrate healthy autoscaling actions for Dedicated-like loads (burst to 2x for 15 minutes).
Safety: Default safety filters are enabled and pass the safety smoke tests defined in safety-evals (no allowed unsafe outputs across a 500-item prompt set).

Observability: Console dashboards expose token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, live eval-score deltas, and per-customer fallback counts — all with retention appropriate for oncall postmortems.

Rollback criteria: Any observed eval metric regression exceeding thresholds, or production error spike > 2x baseline sustained for >= 10 minutes, triggers immediate automated rollback to previous model variant and an incident bridge.
Security & Compliance: SSO auth flows, tenant-isolation headers, and KMS key usage are validated in a security checklist and security review flagged as complete prior to GA.
Docs & SDKs: Public API reference, examples for migration from legacy endpoints, and SDK patches (python/js) merged and published before staged canary begins.
rollout_plan: Pre-canary: Run offline evals against recorded production traffic sample (30M tokens) and a held-out rating set; pass quality gates for 3 consecutive daily runs.
Canary-0 (internal): 0% external traffic — internal customer teams and Redwood integration tests for 48 hours.
Canary-1 (seeded): 0.5% traffic for 24 hours to seeded customers (opt-in list); continuous eval scoring every 15 minutes; automated rollback on gate failure.
Canary-2 (broader): 5% traffic for 48 hours across regions with traffic shaping (latency-sensitive slice + cost-sensitive slice); monitor per-slice metrics and manual review at 24h.
Canary-3 (ramp): 25% traffic for 72 hours with throttled burst windows and A/B quality probes; require engineering sign-off to proceed to GA.
GA: Full rollout after 7 days of stable canary with no regression and completed post-mortem review for any minor issues observed.
decisions: Unify routing: chose a single endpoint surface (mode parameter) rather than multiple distinct endpoints to reduce SDK churn; agreed to keep explicit content-type fields in the request body.
Default caching: ephemeral KV caching enabled at 60s by default with per-tenant override — trade-off accepted between freshness and cost reduction for repetitive prompts.
Model variants: will surface two primary model profiles (high-quality, low-latency) instead of an open catalog at GA to simplify eval coverage and rollout gating.
Quantization: postpone wide quantization options at GA; allow internal beta for select tenants to avoid divergent behavior at launch.
open_questions: Pricing alignment: Should the GA pricing change when routing customers to the new unified surface (cost-per-token vs per-endpoint)? Finance + GTM decision needed.
Determinism: Do we guarantee deterministic seeds for completions when user supplies seed param? This affects caching and eval reproducibility.
Embeddings naming: Do we keep legacy embedding model names for compatibility or issue new v2 names? Existing customers may rely on names in stored vectors.
Migration window: How long do we accept legacy endpoint traffic and what is the deprecation notice period? Product + Support to define.
